text:
Tommy Novak has become one of the quieter good stories in Pittsburgh. The 29-year-old from St. Paul, a third-round pick by Nashville in 2015, has 16 points in 23 games, five of them on the power play, and in his last ten he scored five goals even as the Penguins lost eight of them.

The underlying numbers back him more than the record does. At 5v5 Pittsburgh has taken 56% of the expected goals with him on the ice, four points better than without him. That matches what Evolving-Hockey saw last season, when his teams created 0.24 more expected goals per 60 with him out there (96th percentile among forwards), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 59% of his exits leaving the zone with the puck.

The finishing is the soft spot. He's shooting 20% against a likely range of 12 to 16%, so a few of those goals will dry up. The minutes are drifting up (over 19 in two of the last three games), and that is the thing to watch: a center who tilts the ice like this earns them.
